lines.li: [us] How is {TOWN} faring?
[them] {FORTUNE}, since {FORTUNEWHY}, if you want it plainly.
[us] Is it getting any better?
[them,town:struggling] Not yet, it takes more than one good season to climb out of that.
[them] Ask me again in a season.
[them] My people have been {FORTUNE} since {FORTUNEWHY}, and the elders count every basket.
[us] Is there anything we could send?
[them] Ask the elders, they're too proud to ask you.
[them] {TOWN} has been {FORTUNE} since {FORTUNEWHY}, and the tithe is still the tithe.
[us] Won't your lord ease it?
[them] Lords ease nothing, aye, except their belts at the feast.
[them] {TOWN} has been {FORTUNE} since {FORTUNEWHY}, and prices only go one way.
[us] Up, I suppose.
[them] Up, and wages the other way.
[them] {TOWN} has been {FORTUNE} since {FORTUNEWHY}, and I have the figures to prove it.
[us] I'll take your word for it.
[them] Most people do, nobody likes my figures.
[them] {TOWN} has been {FORTUNE} since {FORTUNEWHY}, though the court prefers not to hear it.
[us] Won't the court help?
[them] The court helps where it will be seen helping, and {TOWN} is a long way from being seen.
[them] Since {FORTUNEWHY}, I sell less at {TOWN} than I do on the road.
[us] Then sell to us.
[them] That's the idea, and I'll be glad of the silver.
[us] {TOWN} seems to be doing well.
[them] {FORTUNE}, and mostly thanks to {FORTUNEWHY}.
[us] Long may it last.
[them,their:tribal] The elders say good seasons are lent, not given.
[them] It won't, these things never do, so we're enjoying it while it does.
[them] Since {FORTUNEWHY} there's silver moving at {TOWN}, and I've brought some of it.
[us] Then let's see you spend it.
[them] Carefully, I didn't come by it by being careless.
[them] Since {FORTUNEWHY} the market at {TOWN} has been fuller than anyone remembers.
[us] And the tithe?
[them] Paid early, which has the reeve worried we're hiding something.
[them] Since {FORTUNEWHY} {TOWN} has had more gifts to give than to ask for.
[us] That's a good place to be.
[them] It is, and the elders say to give while we can.
[them] {TOWN}'s numbers have been up since {FORTUNEWHY}, every one of them.
[us] Even the ones that ought to go down?
[them] Those too, which is the only thing that worries me.
[them] {TOWN} is {FORTUNE}, and for once the people blame me for nothing.
[us] Enjoy it.
[them] I am, quietly, before somebody notices.
[them] People keep turning up at {TOWN} looking for work, and most of them find it.
[us] And the ones who don't?
[them] They move on, or they marry in, whichever comes first.
[them] {TOWN} is {FORTUNE}, and a caravan of ours is already on the road to you.
[us] Then we'd better have something worth selling.
[them] Have silver, mostly, they're bringing plenty to sell.
[them] {TOWN} has never done so well, and I've lived long enough to worry about it.
[us] Worry about doing well?
[them] Good years make people careless, and careless people forget to put things by.
[them] The war's going our way, and {TOWN} is {FORTUNE} in spite of it.
[us] Some would call that lucky.
[them] Some would, but they weren't there.
[them] {FORTUNEWHY} stirred things up at {TOWN}, but it's held steady.
[us] That's no small thing.
[them] No, steady is underrated.
[them] On land like ours, steady is as good as it gets, and we're steady.
[us] Is that enough?
[them,their:tribal] The land gives what it gives, and we take no more.
[them] It has to be, the land won't give more however nicely you ask.
[them] We're {FORTUNE} still, but {ENDED} is over, and the worst is behind us.
[us] Then things can only get better.
[them,their:tribal] Don't say that, the spirits listen.
[them] Don't say that aloud, it never helps.

ColonyCouncil.OutsiderTalkDef.heard: {TOWN} is still {FORTUNE}, but mending now that {ENDED} is over.

lines.li: [them] The war's over and {TOWN} is {FORTUNE}, but at least nobody's marching.
[us] That's something to build on.
[them] It's all we've got to build on, so it'll have to do.
[them] Changing hands cost {TOWN} dearly, and it's {FORTUNE} now.
[us] Will it recover?
[them] Towns do, given a few quiet seasons.
[them] With the war on, {TOWN} is {FORTUNE}, and nobody's surprised.
[us] Does the war reach {TOWN} itself?
[them,war:losing] More every season, we've lost towns already.
[them] Not the fighting, but the prices and the fear, yes.
[them,their:tribal] {TOWN} is {FORTUNE}, and the meat runs out before the moon does.
[them] {TOWN} is {FORTUNE}, and food is the first thing to run short.
[us,colony:plenty] We could spare some, if your people asked.
[us] That's a hard way to live, and I'm sorry for it.
[them] Kind words, and we'll remember them.
[them] {TOWN} is {FORTUNE}, and medicine is the hardest thing of all to find.
[us,colony:hospital] We might spare a little from our {HOSPITAL}, if it came to that.
[us] I hope it doesn't come to the worst.
[them] So do we, every night.
[them] {HEAD} has aged a year every season since {TOWN} fell on hard times.
[us] It's a lot to carry.
[them] It is, and {HEAD} won't let anyone take the other end.
[them] Every family in {TOWN} looks at me when the stores run thin.
[us] That's the burden of leading.
[them] I'd trade it for a full storehouse in a heartbeat.
[them] {TOWN} is {FORTUNE}, and some of ours are already on the road your way.
[us] They'll be welcome.
[them] I hope so, they've had a hard season.
[them] {TOWN} is {FORTUNE}, but we'd sooner tighten our belts than complain.
[us] There's no shame in asking for help.
[them] Tell that to my grandmother.
[us] Is there anything we could do for {TOWN}?
[them,town:short:food] Food, if you have any to spare, nothing else matters as much.
[them,town:short:medicine] Medicine, if you can spare it, the sick come first.
[them] Trade with us fairly and think well of us, that's all I'd ask.
[us] We'll do what we can.
[them] Your stores are fuller than all of {TOWN}'s put together, I'd guess.
[us] We've had a good run.
[them,trait:Greedy] Then you won't miss a little, will you?
[them] Then I hope it lasts, and that you remember who went without.
[them] {TOWN} is {FORTUNE}, and I hear your people are tightening their belts too.
[us] It's a lean time all round.
[them] Then we'll be lean together, and fat together when it turns.
[them] {TOWN} is {FORTUNE}, and our traders will have food to sell if your people are short.
[us] We might take you up on that.
[them] Do, and bring silver, it's still trade.
